tasks.behavior: Tokens sent to the invoice receiver factory or implementation can be returned by the refund authority
acceptance: The factory gets a refund-authority recover(token, to, amount); nobody else can call it, and it can't touch a receiver's money.
Contract tests and the fuzz and invariant suites cover it; docs/contracts/rules.md and operations.md describe it; it ships before the first mainnet deploy.
A receiver's refundable() reads 0 off its intended chain, as factory.status does and refund() allows (audit 2026-11-04); a test covers it.
Money sent to the receiver implementation returns through its recover, for the refund authority only; clones keep every current guard (security review 2026-11-06).
The backend receive-address constants, vectors and canary example match the new factory and implementation.
notes: 2026-11-04 Audit 2026-11-04: InvoiceReceiver.refundable() returns the balance on a wrong chain where refund() reverts. Fix: return 0 when block.chainid != intendedChainId. Any receiver change moves the factory's CREATE2 address (vectors test fails), so it ships with this task's redeploy.
2026-11-05 blocked: Deferred by owner (2026-11-05) to the first mainnet deploy: the refundable() fix moves the factory address, so it ships with that redeploy, with the factory recover.

2026-11-06 review fail by reviewer: Contract code is sound; docs and one test fall short. Security: only the refund authority moves money. Factory recover moves only the factory's own balance: transfer() from the factory, and no receiver has that selector, fallback or receive. The implementation branch (address(this) == self) is unreachable from factory clones, outside clones or delegatecall contexts, because self is the implementation's immutable. Clones still run _onlyClone, terms and the invoice-token guard before any transfer. The implementation's ReentrancyGuard uses its own storage. No new stuck-funds case. Addresses: recomputed factory 0xf93da73F…0dd2, implementation 0x26b7DB22…630f, runtime codehash 0xdca35aa3…9cd1; the e2e RECEIVE and OPTION_RECEIVE equal predict. Old addresses appear only in deployments.json and config_test.go. forge test: 79 pass, 1 skipped. Pay vitest: 48 pass. Go address/config: ok. docs-check: 0 errors. Findings to fix (no contract source change, so addresses stay): (1) docs/diagrams/security-keys.json, the 'who can move money' diagram, is not updated. Edge a14 Safe->factory says only 'pause', and the factory node never mentions recover. The Safe->implementation recover path is missing. docs/contracts/rules.md Status asks for docs/diagrams updates in the same PR. AGENTS.md says a fix covers every place the behavior shows. (2) PLAN.md:147 still lists 'The factory gets a refund-authority recover: tokens sent to it have no way out today' as an open pre-mainnet gap. This PR closes it, and the implementation case too. (3) test/Symbolic.t.sol check_implementationRecoverOnlyByAuthority: assert(token.balanceOf(address(receiver)) == 0) is vacuous, since the receiver gets no deposit. Mint a symbolic deposit to the receiver, as check_factoryRecoverNeverTakesReceiverMoney does. No test covers impl.recover(..., address(0), ...) reverting InvalidDestination. Non-blocking: (4) After merge, address.Factory names an undeployed factory. cmd/api startup (main.go:67, FactoryDeployed through chain.CheckEnabled) then refuses to start on staging. settle.go:212, returns.go:148 and stray.go:164 reject old-factory testnet invoices. Promote to staging only after the testnet redeploy and the deployments.json update. (5) Nits: forge lint now flags arbitrary-send-eth at InvoiceReceiver.sol:137 (_send), because the authority check sits in the caller. rules.md:57-58 is one sentence of about 29 words (D-84 limit 25).
